title: Francis of Paola (2 April)
hookLine: a hermit whose motto was charity, who named his brothers the least

lines: A DYING KING SENDS FOR A HERMIT.
HE GOES ONLY WHEN THE POPE ASKS.
cards: A dying king sends for a hermit. The king is Louis the Eleventh of France, powerful, frightened and sick. He has heard that a holy man in the south of Italy works wonders, and he wants one.
He sends messengers, gifts, promises. The hermit, a man named Francis from the little town of Paola, doesn't want to go. He goes only when the pope tells him to.
He makes the long journey to France, walks into the royal court in his rough habit, and stands at the bedside of a king who wants a miracle. What he gives him is something else.

teach.b: Francis didn't cure the king. Tradition says he stayed with him, prayed with him, and helped him get ready to die in peace.
Then he stayed on in France for the rest of his own life, and, tradition says, the French court kept asking his advice. To see why that matters, go back to the start.

teach.h: A HERMIT IN A CAVE BY THE SEA.
teach.b: As a young man Francis went off alone to live as a hermit in a cave near the sea. Other young men came to join him, and slowly a community grew.

teach.h: THE MINIMS: THE LEAST OF ALL.
teach.b: He gave them a name meant to keep them low: the Minims. Tradition says he chose it to mean the least of all, lower even than Francis of Assisi's Friars Minor, the lesser brothers.

teach.h: ONE WORD ON THE BADGE: CHARITY.
teach.b: And he gave them one word as a motto, written on their badge: Charity. Love. The Minims kept a life of Lent all year round, with no meat and plain food, not to be grim, but to stay light and free for others.
Behind the name sits a line from Matthew's Gospel, where Jesus speaks of the hungry, the stranger, the sick and the prisoner.

teach.h: ONE OF THESE MY LEAST BRETHREN.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "Amen I say to you, as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me." The least ones are where Christ says he will be found.
Francis wanted his brothers among them, not above them. Even in a palace. The hermit at the king's bed was there as the least man in the room.

how: Catholics keep Francis of Paola's optional memorial on 2 April; the Minim friars, nuns and lay members who follow his rule still keep a Lenten diet all year.

games.q: you're Francis, a hermit. a dying king begs you to come and heal him, with gifts and promises. the pope says go. you reach his bed. what do you do?
o: stay with him and help him prepare to die.
take the gifts and go home.
games.why: tradition says he didn't cure the king. he stayed, prayed with him, and helped him die in peace, then stayed on in France.

practice: Ask yourself what the smallest, least noticed job around you is: the dishes nobody wants, the bin at the curb, the coworker everyone talks past. Hold one of them in mind, a least thing, done without needing anyone to notice.
If you pray, offer it with the word on the Minims' badge, charity; if you don't, simply hold the task in mind.

wordCard.voice: Minims, the least brothers, founded by Francis of Paola. A hermit who gave them charity as their motto, and sat at a dying king's bed.
